A table of its own for each application chosen, appcontrol_ and its name, holding servers it was seen with. Every nDPI category has a table without being chosen: appcontrol_cat_ and its name. The list is the installed nDPI's.
Allow access to application control: applications nDPI names, firewall aliases it fills, and its settings
An independent project, not affiliated with Deciso B.V.
Connections: named by nDPI from their packets since the classifier started. Guessed: named by port or address only, never put in a table. Each connection counts once, in the window it began in.
Each table is an External alias in Firewall: Aliases, for a rule's source or destination: servers nDPI named, each kept until unseen for the address expiry. Nothing is blocked by this plugin yet.
How long an address stays in a table once unseen: the Expire of the tables' aliases, carried out by OPNsense's own cron. Seen again, its time starts again.

Name each connection's application with nDPI and keep the servers it names in pf tables, aliases in Firewall: Aliases. It reads a copy of what the firewall sees and changes no traffic. Off, the classifier stops and its aliases leave Firewall: Aliases - switched off instead where a rule or a setting still names one.

Not named: nDPI could not say what a connection is. Guessed: named by port or address only. No application: nDPI named its protocol - TLS, QUIC or HTTP - and no application on top. Not named and No application list only connections whose beginning was seen. Server name and JA4 fingerprint are what its client sent first, to tell where it comes from; JA4 is read from TLS over TCP only. Latest 500 of each kind kept.
Where connections are read. None chosen: every internal interface - one with an address of its own and no gateway. No port is made promiscuous.
nDPI is not installed: package ndpi is needed.
os-xgs-npu is installed: each connection is classified from its first packets, seen by the host before it moves into hardware.
pf alone holds these tables: without os-xgs-npu no hardware takes part.
windows cut short: connections past the packets, connections or bytes a window reads were not classified
